solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reformed individual to move into a lower gear

definitions.text: to move into a lower gear

parts.note: someone reformed has changed their ways
own, as in one's own, individual to oneself

explanation.surface: A reformed character takes things more slowly, like a driver shifting into a lower gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing down is the driving phrase for shifting the gearbox to a lower ratio.

clue.text: One who applauds directors finding filmmaking equipment

parts.note: a clapper is one who claps
a board is the group of directors of a company

explanation.surface: An applauding spectator finds directors on a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directors' suggests film directors; here it means a company board.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapperboard is the hinged board snapped at the start of each film take to sync sound and picture.

clue.text: Stroll accomplished covering miles

indicators.note: the word for accomplished goes over and around the other letter

parts.note: an accomplished person is able, skilled

explanation.surface: An expert walker covers the miles at an easy pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace, the same as strolling.

clue.text: Make fun of crude effigy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to mock or tease
second meaning: the stuffed figure of ... Fawkes burned on Bonfire Night in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: Bonfire Night (5 November) in Britain burns a homemade figure of the plotter Guy Fawkes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for ridiculing someone and a noun for the stuffed Fawkes figure.

clue.text: Want expensive trough cleaned out

parts.note: dear means costly, expensive

indicators.note: the inside of the word is emptied, leaving just its outer letters

explanation.surface: A farmer wants a pricey trough emptied and scrubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb of desire, but it is the noun for lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want here is the noun for lack or scarcity, which dearth means.

clue.text: Rain on outbuilding — dirty film seen after this?

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky
a shed is a small outbuilding

explanation.surface: Rain falls on the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9pm watershed in British broadcasting is the time after which adult material may be shown.
explanation.definitionFit: On UK television the watershed is the evening time before which programmes unsuitable for children are banned.

clue.text: Streak of light encountered upset small deer

parts.note: met means encountered

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a roe is a small European deer

explanation.surface: A walker met a startled little deer, and it bolted like a flash.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a shooting star, seen as a bright trail across the night sky.

clue.text: Bar, with five couples, disheartened older male singer

parts.note: a counter is the bar across which drinks are served
five pairs make ten

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letters, is taken away, leaving the outside

explanation.surface: In a bar, five dancing couples sadden an ageing male vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'older' looks like part of the definition, but losing its heart leaves OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A countertenor is a male voice singing in the alto range, above the tenor.

clue.text: Religious building always full of books, European

indicators.note: the word for always is filled with the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: ay is an old and poetic word for always
B is the abbreviation for book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: A church or monastery perpetually stocked with European books.
explanation.walkthrough: Ay for always is old or poetic, surviving in phrases like 'for ever and ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a monastery or the church attached to one, a building for religious life.

clue.text: Style of design poorly rated by company

indicators.note: letters doing poorly are out of shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A design style that critics rated poorly, according to some firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' reads as a verdict on the style, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is the geometric decorative movement of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Bill interrupted by Greek character, one who writes abject verses

indicators.note: the poster is broken into by the Greek letter, which goes inside it

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice or poster
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill keeps being interrupted by a Greek person while composing dreadful poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; here it is a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is a contemptuous term for an inferior, pretentious writer of poetry.

clue.text: Classical goddess quiet during the radio broadcast

indicators.note: the quiet letter comes during, so inside, the other letters
broadcast also means scattered, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A myth is told quietly over a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges THE RADIO, and P goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Heroin used regularly for a long time

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word is used, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Someone has been taking heroin habitually for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of Heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long period, often an age of geological history.

clue.text: Unrefined rot mostly: that's disgusting!

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: ugh is the exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a piece as crude nonsense, exclaiming in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rot' reads as part of the definition's sense of rubbish, but it is fodder to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough means crude or not finished, lacking polish, as in a rough draft.

clue.text: A French congregation spread out

parts.note: un is the French for a
a church's congregation is its fold, its flock

explanation.surface: A French church congregation fans out.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfold is to open out or extend something folded, so to spread it.

clue.text: Some author describes crowd

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer depicts a throng of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large, often unruly mass of people.

clue.text: Esme dead slow, each time cutting half grassland tract

indicators.note: half of each of the three words is cut away, its front half

explanation.surface: Esme, dead slow, ambles through a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the back half of each word: ME, AD and OW.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a field of grass, often cut for hay.

clue.text: Oscar, a loud idiot

parts.note: Oscar is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for O
F stands for forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: Someone calls a man named Oscar a noisy fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, stupid person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Amount owed concerning doctor at the back

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
aft is the nautical word for towards the rear of a vessel

explanation.surface: A bill relates to a doctor's practice round the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is the sum owed to a bank after spending beyond the account balance.

clue.text: People from Denmark, moving first to middle range of mountains

indicators.note: the first letter is moved into the middle of the word

parts.note: Danes are people from Denmark

explanation.surface: Danish people head to a middling mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the first letter of DANES, moves to the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes is the mountain range running down western South America.

clue.text: Finally, Manchester United recovered

indicators.note: finally picks the very end, the last letter of the next word

parts.note: allied means joined together, united

explanation.surface: A football report: at last Manchester United came back into the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manchester United' reads as the football club, but it splits into the last letter of Manchester and a synonym for united.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallied means recovered strength or rebounded, as a team or a share price does.

clue.text: Expand Caribbean retreat

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies, the Caribbean islands
a den is a private retreat or study

explanation.surface: Someone plans to extend their Caribbean holiday hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen is to make broader, a synonym for expanding something.

clue.text: Present mounted and secured

indicators.note: in a down answer, mounted means the word climbs upward, reading backwards

parts.note: now is the present time

explanation.surface: A gift is put on display and fixed in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests a gift; it is the present moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Won means gained or obtained, as in won a contract, which secured means.

clue.text: Cheese and wine given to royal family

parts.note: red is short for red wine
Windsor is the surname of the British royal family

explanation.surface: Cheese and wine are served to the royals.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Windsor is an English cheddar marbled with red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Windsor is a British cheese, cheddar veined with red wine or port.
